chunks: “And an abandoned well and a lofty palace.”
He said: “The abandoned well is the silent Imam, and the lofty palace is the speaking Imam.”
And Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated it from al-ʿAmrakī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, similarly.

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ الصَّامِتُ: the silent Imam, an Imam not outwardly manifest in public proclamation
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ النَّاطِقُ: the speaking Imam, an Imam openly expressing and establishing guidance
key_terms.بِئْرٍ مُعَطَّلَةٍ: an abandoned well, interpreted here as the silent Imam
key_terms.قَصْرٍ مَشِيدٍ: a lofty or strongly built palace, interpreted here as the speaking Imam
key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: similar to it; indicating a parallel transmission of the same meaning

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the abandoned well and lofty palace in Shia tafsir?
ai.summary: This narration gives an esoteric explanation of the Qur'anic image of an abandoned well and a lofty palace. It identifies the abandoned well as the silent Imam and the lofty palace as the speaking Imam, indicating ranks of divinely appointed authority and guidance.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Al Hassan and Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Musa Bin Al Qasim Al Bajaly, (It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’farasws, from his brotherasws Musaasws regarding the Words of the Exalted [22:45] and an abandoned well and a constructed palace (deserted),

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘The abandoned well is the silent Imam<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, and the constructed palace (deserted) is the speaking Imam<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>’.
And it is reported by Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky, from Ali son of Ja’farasws, from Abu Al Hassanasws, similar to it.
en.sarwar: 75. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Hakam ibn al-Buhlul from a man frm abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about the words of Allah, the Most High. ““It has been revealed to you and to those who lived before you that if you consider other things equal to God, your deeds will be made devoid of all virtue. .” [39:65].
The Imam (a.s.) said, “It means equal in Wilaya.” “(Muhammad), You must worship God alone and give Him thanks.” [39:66].
The Imam (a.s.) said, “It means worship Allah through obedience and be thankful if I provided you support through your brother, your cousin.”
